rv.q: The Roundabout Theatre Company's exceptionally charming revival of The Robber Bridegroom is exactly the kind of intimate extravaganza you would expect from

Timbers draws from his usual bag of magic tricks, prop jokes, unexpected taxidermy, and winking meta-theatricality to keep the eye and attention engaged at all times. Even so, the story, having been pulled away from any real engagement with its dark fundamentals, now seems like an excuse instead of the point.
Director Alex Timbers has turned genres gleefully on their edges with "Bloody Bloody Andrew Jackson" and "Here Lies Love."
Even without his name on the program, it would be a cinch to pick The Robber Bridegroom as the work of Alex Timbers.
The production is directed with atmospheric flare and nonstop playfulness by Alex Timbers.

Leslie Kritzer puts on a Norma Desmond-like façade as Rosamund's jealous and lustful stepmom, Salome, singing with soaring pipes and nailing every laugh with the kind of physical zaniness reminiscent of old-school giants like Carol Burnett and Lucille Ball.

With its mismatched lovers wandering in a forest, with a potential husband unrecognizable only because he wears a bit of smeared berry on his face, with its Rosamund (which sounds almost like Rosalind), Timbers's take on Robber Bridegroom seems like nothing so much as a goofy spoof of Shakespeare. Which is fun!

cn.t: Alex Timbers' playful revival showcases strong performances, especially Leslie Kritzer's scene-stealing turn, but critics find his hyperkinetic directorial style suffocates the material, leaving this forgotten musical charming yet unessential.

vs.sum: The Samuel J. Friedman Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions and a well-raked mezzanine, ensuring a clear view from most seats. The sound quality is consistently praised, and the seating is comfortable with decent legroom. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant design following renovation, though facilities like restrooms are average, leading to some congestion during intermissions.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Built-in induction loop for t-coil hearing aids.
